desc:
Given an array nums of positive integers and an integer limit, choose three elements at three different positions so that their sum is as large as possible but not greater than limit.

Return that sum, or -1 if every triple sums to more than limit (or there are fewer than three elements).

nums = [5, 2, 7, 3, 10, 1], limit = 15
10 + 3 + 2 = 15
result = 15

nums = [4, 6, 9], limit = 18
result = -1
hints: Trying every triple is O(n³). After fixing one element, the task becomes a pair problem on the rest.
Sort the array. Fix the smallest index i. The remaining question is: best pair among indices after i with sum at most limit - nums[i].
For the pair, use lo = i + 1, hi = n - 1. If the triple sum fits, record it and move lo up; otherwise move hi down.
editorial: Sort the array, then for each first element a[i] look for the best pair in a[i+1:] with the two-pointer sweep: if a[i] + a[lo] + a[hi] ≤ limit, this is a candidate and a[lo] cannot do better with any other partner (all larger partners were already rejected or are not larger), so advance lo; otherwise a[hi] is too large even with the smallest available partner, so retreat hi.

The outer loop has n choices and each sweep is linear, so the time is O(n²) after the sort. Exiting early when the sum equals limit exactly, or when the three smallest remaining values already exceed it, is only an optimization.
